top.description: SSC Napoli v Torino FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Kevin De Bruyne has hit out at the Italian media for creating a hostile environment for his family amid ongoing speculation regarding his future at Napoli. The Belgian playmaker spoke out ahead of a highly anticipated return to the Etihad Stadium for a Champions League encounter with his former club, Manchester City. Frustration over privacy and transfer links De Bruyne has expressed his deep frustration with recent reports suggesting he could leave the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in the January transfer window . The veteran playmaker, who has been linked with a move to PSV Eindhoven, used his pre-match press conference to address a recent interview given by his wife in Belgium that he feels was intentionally misinterpreted by the Italian press to fuel exit rumours. "I’m quite sorry about it all to be honest. If you go and read the article, which you have not read, you will understand what she said. I was away in Belgium and then a lot of things were being said and there were a lot of negative reactions towards my wife," De Bruyne said, as quoted by Football Italia . He voiced specific anger over the publication of photos of his private residence, adding, "I saw photos of my house in the press, which is not good. I know that journalists in Italy have created this situation and I don’t know why. You do not know my private life, you have no right to comment on my private life. It was an unpleasant situation for me and my wife." The veteran playmaker tight-lipped on Napoli future De Bruyne has remained tight-lipped over his long-term future with Napoli, admitting that his approaching 36th birthday leaves him with plenty to weigh up amid his ongoing contract situation . Despite the uncertainty surrounding his next move, the veteran midfielder insisted his focus remains firmly on giving everything for the Partenopei. Rather than getting drawn into speculation, the Belgian playmaker stressed that his immediate priority is maintaining his strong form and helping the club navigate a demanding campaign. top.title: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia, bipolar disorder
top.description: Former world heavyweight boxing champion, Tyson Fury, has disclosed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a forthcoming Netflix documentary about his life and career. According to Deadline , Fury made the revelation in the feature-length documentary titled Tyson Fury , which is scheduled for release later this month. The boxer said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia shortly after defeating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 to become the world heavyweight champion. He also disclosed that he received a bipolar disorder diagnosis in 2017. Reflecting on his mental health struggles in the documentary, Fury described experiencing periods of severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much,” he reportedly said. Fury also recounted experiencing intense anxiety that frequently woke him in the middle of the night. He said he eventually sought professional help from a psychiatrist in London, who assessed him through a series of questions and identified depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder. The documentary also features contributions from his wife, Paris Fury, and father, John Fury, who discuss his mental health challenges. top.description: Stats: Here’s how Barcelona have fared without Lamine Yamal in the squad Hansi Flick will face his first Barcelona match without Lamine Yamal this season when the Catalans travel to Azerbaijan to meet Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday, November 25. The 19-year-old winger has been ruled out because of mild discomfort in his right ankle, with the club confirming that his absence is a precautionary measure and that he is expected to return against Deportivo on Sunday. Yamal’s absence ends an uninterrupted run of 17 appearances in Barcelona’s official matches this season, having accumulated 1,445 minutes, scoring 13 goals and providing 13 assists. However, the German manager has previous experience managing without his most influential young forward, and Barcelona’s results suggest the squad has gradually become better equipped to cope with his absence. Barcelona’s record without Lamine Yamal under Hansi Flick Since Flick took charge, Barcelona have played 17 matches without Yamal, recording 11 victories, five defeats and one draw. During the 2024/25 campaign, Barcelona struggled to maintain consistency without their right winger. They won just two of five matches, beating Brest 3-0 in the Champions League and Barbastro 4-0 in the Copa del Rey. The remaining three fixtures exposed their difficulties, as defeats against Real Sociedad and Atletico Madrid, alongside a draw against Celta Vigo, left Flick with limited reasons for optimism when his teenage forward was unavailable. Barcelona improved considerably during the 2025/26 season The picture changed significantly in 2025/26 when Barcelona collected nine victories from the 12 matches Yamal missed. Notably, their ability to produce positive results without him was particularly evident before his season-ending injury in April. Flick’s side defeated Newcastle United, Valencia, Getafe, Real Oviedo and Slavia Prague during earlier spells without the winger. Sevilla provided a notable exception, handing Barcelona a 1-4 defeat. top.title: Agit Kabayel is the ringmaster of a new heavyweight circus
top.description: There was a time when an American was in one corner of every single heavyweight world-title fight. Every fight from the end of the bare-knuckle period to the end of the 1980s. The fall of the Wall and the arrival of the Eastern Bloc boxers changed the landscape forever, but still Americans held the grip on a title that seemed forever destined to be owned by a man from Philadelphia or Houston or Louisville. That is all over now, possibly gone for good. Deontay Wilder was the last American heavyweight world champion, and he was beaten in seven rounds by Tyson Fury in early 2020; he challenged Fury the following year, lost again, and that was the last time an American came anywhere near the world heavyweight title. Agit Kabayel after stopping Zhilei Zhang in early 2025 (Getty) Close to 30 years ago, Don King announced that he was searching for the next American heavyweight superstar; that desperate search is continuing today, and at the same time gyms in Tirana, Moscow and Lagos are full of heavyweight dreamers. This Saturday, in front of 50,000 fans in Dusseldorf , Germany’s Agit Kabayel defends his WBC heavyweight title when he meets the unbeaten Nelson Hysa of Albania. It is a bizarrely cosmopolitan clash. Kabayel, on his way directly to the WBC title, stopped in succession a Russian, a Chinese fighter, a Croatian, a Pole, and a Cuban. There is not an American heavyweight left to come even close to pushing Kabayel. The top American is arguably a man called Michael Hunter, who is 38 and had his best win in 2018. Hunter is the only American worth a top-20 ranking, and he is lost in a turbulent sea of boxers from a dozen countries. A Nigerian, an Australian and about seven British boxers are in front of Hunter. Where is Rocky Balboa when you need him? Right now, Kabayel might just be the best of the four heavyweight champions, with Daniel Dubois , Filip Hrgovic and Murat Gassiev holding the other belts in the wake of Oleksandr Usyk giving up all of the gold . top.title: The Davis Cup is broken but Carlos Alcaraz can save it
top.description: For nearly five months of this year, Carlos Alcaraz was sidelined, nursing a wrist injury which threatened to derail his entire season. Just three months on from his return, and despite managing two different injury concerns, the Spaniard has rewritten the history books and could yet send another record tumbling before signing off for Christmas. Four days after claiming his first ATP Finals title, becoming the youngest man – at just 23 – to complete the clean sweep of all four majors and the season-ending individual crown, he could join only Andre Agassi , Novak Djokovic , and Roger Federer in the pantheon of greats to also win the Davis Cup . The tennis calendar doesn’t so much slow to a halt over Christmas as barrel almost cleanly through into the next season, with a rapid turnaround for those heading from the ATP Finals in Turin to the Davis Cup in Bologna this week. But despite Alcaraz’s frenetic autumn schedule, winning three back-to-back tournaments in Vienna, Paris, and Turin, and the wear and tear on his body, he is in spellbinding form and highly fancied to lead Spain to a first title since 2019. The Davis Cup has struggled for relevance in recent years. The fact that it takes place annually lowers the stakes and drama of what claims to be the ‘World Cup’ of tennis, while the torturously convoluted system of play-offs and qualifying ties makes it difficult for the casual fan to understand. Add to that top players’ reluctance to risk injury, and their prioritising of the ATP Tour in an utterly relentless calendar, means the big names tend to drop out and viewers’ interest follows the same downward curve. So it is a huge boost to the tournament that although home star Jannik Sinner remains a long-term absentee, Alcaraz, who missed last year’s Finals, is back, while the Italians – led again by Flavio Cobolli – are fielding a raft of top names including Matteo Berrettini and Lorenzo Musetti . In total, nine top-10 players across both singles and doubles will take part, and seven of the singles top-20. Three-time defending champions Italy face underdogs South Korea before taking on either Felix Auger-Aliassime ’s Canada or Czechia, spearheaded by the top-20 pairing of Jakub Mensik and Jiri Lehecka. The bottom half sees Germany and Spain take on Great Britain and Austria respectively. GB are playing their last tie under the leadership of Leon Smith , who will end a near-17 year stint as captain after this week . There are no faces left from the Finals-winning squad of 2015, the zenith of Smith’s tenure, but there is an exciting mix of the old and new: this year’s breakout British star, Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery , alongside stalwart Cameron Norrie . Most significantly, GB possess a lethal doubles partnership in world No 1 Henry Patten and No 3 Neal Skupski , who between them have won three of the last four Grand Slams. top.title: 49ers win in Mexico and Bills stay top - NFL week 11
top.description: The San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills remain the pacesetters in each conference of the NFL after both won again. The 49ers beat the Minnesota Vikings in the last of a record nine international games this season to take their record to 9-1. They lead the way in the NFC, with the Chicago Bears and their divisional rivals the Detroit Lions next best on 8-2. Buffalo improved to 9-1 for the first time since 1991 and lead the AFC from another pair of divisional rivals, with the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on 8-2. The Cincinnati Bengals are 7-3 after being undone by a walk-off field goal for the Washington Commanders. 49ers outsmart Vikings defence Mexico hosted the first regular-season game to be played outside the US in October 2005, and the NFL returned to the country on Sunday following a four-year absence. After being redeveloped for the 2026 World Cup, the Azteca Stadium staged its sixth NFL game and the third involving San Francisco, who kicked off this season's international series by beating the Los Angeles Rams in Australia in week one. Sunday's game pitted the league's best offence against the best defence and was the first international game to be played in the primetime slot. The Vikings defence had not conceded more than 23 points in a game this season, but the 49ers offence outsmarted them in front of 85,612 fans in Mexico City. The 49ers scored four touchdowns in the first half - two by George Kittle - before running out 35-10 winners. Mike Evans returned after missing three games with an Achilles problem to finish with 109 receiving yards and a touchdown. With the game played at high altitude - about 7,220ft (2,240m) above sea level - some players used oxygen masks on the sidelines. San Francisco face another test of their Super Bowl credentials next Sunday at home to the defending champions, the 6-4 Seattle Seahawks, who were one of six teams on their bye this week. San Francisco linebacker Fred Warner has Mexican heritage and his first name is Federico [Getty Images] Giants secure statement win The Jacksonville Jaguars entered week 11 with the best regular-season record over the past 12 months - they had lost only twice - and had scored more than 30 points in each of their past four games. Yet the New York Giants managed to stifle the Jaguars for three quarters and led 20-6 heading into what proved to be a dramatic final quarter. The Jaguars had to settle for a field goal after a controversial call denied them a touchdown, but they still threatened a fightback as they cut the deficit to five. The Giants offence did enough to stop the Jags getting one more possession, though, and secure a 23-18 home win. It was the first time the NFC East leaders have beaten a team with a winning record this season and they are now 6-3-1, while the 7-3 Jags remain in charge of the AFC South. top.description: The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, has said the massive turnout at the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State demonstrates the people’s acceptance of the party despite what he described as campaigns of calumny and insults against it. Yari said the APC was consolidating its support base to secure victory at all levels in the 2027 general elections, attributing the party’s growing acceptance to its closeness to the masses. He stated this on Monday during the APC campaign flag-off held in Talata-Mafara, which attracted party faithful, support groups and members of the public. All Progressives Congress governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State on Monday, November 23, 2026. Crowds of party supporters welcomed Governor Dauda Lawal’s motorcade to Talata-Mafara town before proceeding to the town’s Eid ground, venue of the rally. Speaking at the event, Senator Yari said the large turnout reflected the enthusiasm and commitment of party members and supporters towards the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections. “Make sure this message gets to the public: we are determined to deliver victory for the APC, from President Tinubu down to members of the State House of Assembly. “The overwhelming response to our call demonstrates that, despite the insults and campaigns against the APC, the people of Zamfara have understood our message and are firmly behind the party,” he said. Whenever I turn around and see this mammoth crowd of supporters, I am filled with gratitude. “At this point, I will simply say, let us wait for election day and, ultimately, the swearing-in day,” Lawal said. top.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA launches nighttime evacuation gangs
top.description: …Plans over 10 regional offices ahead of Yuletide By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) has launched a nighttime waste evacuation operation across the state to tackle mounting refuse heaps and restore environmental sanitation ahead of the Christmas and New Year festivities. The exercise, which commenced on Monday night, began along the Isheri–Igando–LASU–Iba corridor, with sanitation teams and heavy-duty equipment deployed to clear identified waste black spots. LAWMA’s Acting Managing Director, Olajuwon Akinyemi, led the operation at Igando Bus Stop alongside the Acting Executive Director of Operations, Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director of Finance, Kunle Adebiyi. Speaking during the exercise, Akinyemi said the nighttime evacuation would be extended to other major entry routes and high-traffic corridors, including Ojota–Ikorodu Road, Mushin–Moshalashi axis and Lekki–Ajah corridor. He said the operation was aimed at restoring Lagos’s environmental appeal and providing a cleaner and healthier atmosphere for residents and visitors expected in the state during the busy December holiday season. To prevent cleared locations from becoming refuse dumps again, the agency said it was partnering with traditional institutions across the state to strengthen community monitoring and enforcement. Beyond the immediate clean-up exercise, Akinyemi announced plans to establish more than 10 regional offices across Lagos as part of efforts to decentralise the authority’s operations. He described the restructuring as non-negotiable, saying the regional offices would improve operational coordination, bring waste management services closer to communities, strengthen accountability and ensure faster responses to sanitation challenges. The LAWMA boss appealed to residents to remain patient with the state government as it works to address waste management challenges across the metropolis. He also urged residents to promptly report service failures by Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators through the authority’s official communication channels to enable it to enforce compliance. Monday night’s win was a product of several factors, one of which was Luka Doncic ‘s sustained offensive brilliance . With 28 points, four rebounds, eight assists, and a steal, the Lakers’ superstar led the winning effort. Even so, one could argue that this win belonged to the role players. The grit and hustle shown by players like Jake LaRavia , Matisse Thybulle , Ziaire Williams , and Collin Sexton at key moments defined the Lakers’ performance. During his postgame press conference , head coach JJ Redick had to acknowledge this. top.description: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the killing of four persons in Ughelli, Delta State, following an outbreak of political violence, calling on security agencies to arrest and prosecute those responsible. Keyamo, in a statement issued on Monday, described the incident in his hometown as disturbing and said several other persons sustained injuries and were receiving treatment. He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished those injured a speedy recovery. The minister also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator allegedly by supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice. “I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” he said. Keyamo lamented that Delta, which had enjoyed relative political peace since 1999, was witnessing a disturbing rise in violence, insisting that political disagreements should not degenerate into killings. “Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence,” he said. He also criticised the slogan, “Rig and Die”, allegedly promoted by some political actors in Delta State and elsewhere, describing it as capable of escalating political tension and encouraging violence. The minister urged those promoting the slogan to reconsider their position, publicly withdraw it and apologise for overheating the political atmosphere. “Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country. As can be seen, anyone can be a victim,” he said. Keyamo maintained that only law enforcement agencies had the authority to deal with offenders, warning political leaders against encouraging their supporters to attack other citizens. nigeria.description: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the killing of four persons in Ughelli, Delta State, following an outbreak of political violence, calling on security agencies to arrest and prosecute those responsible. Keyamo, in a statement issued on Monday, described the incident in his hometown as disturbing and said several other persons sustained injuries and were receiving treatment. He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished those injured a speedy recovery. The minister also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator allegedly by supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice. “I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” he said. Keyamo lamented that Delta, which had enjoyed relative political peace since 1999, was witnessing a disturbing rise in violence, insisting that political disagreements should not degenerate into killings. “Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence,” he said. He also criticised the slogan, “Rig and Die”, allegedly promoted by some political actors in Delta State and elsewhere, describing it as capable of escalating political tension and encouraging violence. The minister urged those promoting the slogan to reconsider their position, publicly withdraw it and apologise for overheating the political atmosphere. “Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country. Fani-Kayode spoke on Monday after meeting with the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja. He said the meeting was part of his official responsibilities and had nothing to do with reports circulating on social media that he had been recalled. “There have been reports on social media suggesting that I have been recalled. The envoy explained that his visit was to submit official reports, consult with ministry officials, spend time with his family and prepare for their possible relocation to South Africa. Concerns have been raised on both sides in a professional diplomatic manner, and no reprimand of any kind occurred,” he said. The high commissioner reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening diplomatic relations between Nigeria and South Africa, particularly in trade, investment and other areas of mutual interest. “I believe strongly that if South Africa and Nigeria do not come together, it would affect the destiny of the whole African continent. nigeria.title: It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege
nigeria.description: Senator Omo-Agege, has alleged that the attack on his campaign train in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State was “premeditated”, saying it was part of an ongoing attempt to eliminate him. Speaking on Channels TV via Zoom, Omo-Agege said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others were critically injured when gunmen opened fire during his campaign event in Udu-Ere, Ughelli North. He said he was addressing supporters when the gunmen opened fire, adding that he heard them repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him. He said he survived the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services, DSS, security details. He said the attack occurred less than five minutes after he began his remarks at the campaign venue. His words: “This is premeditated. It is not something that just happened today. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started. The former Deputy Senate President said four members of his campaign organisation were killed in the attack, including former Federal Character Commissioner, and the immediate past president of the Urhobo Progress Union youth wing. The former senator said he heard the attackers shouting in English, “Omo-Agege, we want to kill,” while the shooting was ongoing. Omo-Agege called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, saying he did not expect the Delta State Police Command to deliver justice. “We are appealing to the IGP to step in immediately and directly handle this investigation. We need justice,” he said. We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” he said. nigeria.title: Police arrest eight suspected drug dealers in Jigawa
nigeria.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested eight suspected drug dealers and consumers, including two women aged 18 and 20, during operations targeting illicit drug trafficking and substance abuse across the state. The arrests were disclosed in a statement issued to newsmen by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Shiisu Lawan Adam. Adam identified the suspects as Garba Sabo, 20; Kamal Ibrahim, 20; Muhammad Ibrahim, 25; Muhammad Nura, 25; Muhammad Bako, 25; Habu Usman, 23, also known as Makwa; Firdausi Sani, 20; and Nusaiba Ibrahim, 18. According to the statement, the suspects, aged between 18 and 25, were arrested at different locations, including Gadama, Bulangu, Sara, Gumel and Kazaure towns. One of the female suspects was identified as a resident of Sandamu Daura in Katsina State. During the operations, the police recovered 8,739 assorted illicit drug-related substances, including suspected Indian hemp, tramadol, pregabalin, diazepam and other intoxicating substances. The recovered exhibits included 4,035 pieces of Exol, 1,384 pieces of D5, 634 pregabalin capsules, 896 tramadol capsules, 248 diazepam tablets and 1,199 wraps of marijuana, alongside three and a half blocks of the substance. Other items recovered included rubber solution, whisky, shisha, syrups, snuff and other intoxicating substances. The Commissioner of Police, CP Tijjani Murtala, said the command would sustain its operations against drug trafficking and substance abuse, warning those involved in the illicit trade to desist or face prosecution. He said the police would continue to deploy intelligence-led policing, surveillance and targeted operations to dismantle drug distribution networks and tackle criminal activities associated with substance abuse. The commissioner also called on parents, guardians, community leaders and religious institutions to intensify efforts to discourage drug abuse, particularly among young people. nigeria.title: Troops kill two bandits, recover rifles in Kogi operation
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two armed bandits and recovered two AK-47 rifles and other items during an intelligence-led ambush operation in Asungwe Forest, Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State. According to a statement by Col. Appolonia Anele, the operation followed sustained offensives against banditry and kidnapping gangs in the state. The statement said the operation was conducted on Monday, November 23, 2026, by troops of the 12 Brigade under Operation Bem Hembe, in conjunction with other hybrid forces. It added that the operation was launched following credible intelligence obtained from previously arrested bandits, which provided actionable leads on the movement of criminal elements operating in Asungwe Forest and adjoining communities along the boundaries of Kogi, Edo and Ondo states. Acting on the intelligence, troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba and positioned themselves along a suspected bandits’ crossing route within the forest. The troops subsequently made contact with the criminals and engaged them with superior firepower, neutralising two bandits, while others fled. Items recovered during the operation included two AK-47 rifles, three magazines, 27 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, two Android phones, three Tecno keypad phones, assorted drugs and bags suspected to belong to the fleeing criminals. The statement said the operation demonstrated the Nigerian Army’s resolve to dismantle criminal networks, disrupt bandits’ movements and deny terrorists and kidnappers freedom of action across vulnerable communities. It added that the Army remained committed to intensifying intelligence-driven operations and sustaining pressure on criminal elements to enhance the security of lives and property. nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae One of the supporters killed in the alleged assassination attempt on former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, was a father of just six months, having welcomed his first child on May 15, 2026. In the emotional post, Umukoro narrated his experience during his wife’s labour, describing women as heroes for enduring the pains of childbirth. Sadly, six months after celebrating the arrival of his newborn son, Umukoro was found dead in his Toyota Highlander SUV following the alleged assassination attempt during a campaign tour by Omo-Agege in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. In a video seen by Vanguard, Umukoro was found lying lifeless in the vehicle, dressed in a white shirt and black shorts. Four persons were confirmed dead in the attack, which occurred during a political campaign activity in the community. In his May 15 Facebook post announcing the birth of his son, Umukoro wrote: “My Prince is here, mother and child in good health. Women are the heroes and keepers of life. “From 1cm to 10cm dilation, I stood firmly beside her through every painful minute that almost felt like a whole year suspended in time between hope and fear. “Indeed, women are heroes. They carry the deepest pains of this world in silence and strength. “I watched my beautiful wife grumble and tremble in agony, entering a realm where shame no longer existed. She tore off her clothes, choosing nakedness as though, in that vulnerable state, she found the strength to fight a battle nature designed only for mothers. “Every single minute mattered to us. I kept staring at my phone, counting contractions, wishing with all my heart that I could take the pain away from her. But each time I thought the worst had passed, the pain returned even harder. business.title: Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change. The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged. Share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases. Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the company raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million , with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million. Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The dollar index rose about 0.65% to 104.40 , its strongest level since April 2025, as the stock rebound put more Federal Reserve rate hikes back in play. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, pointed to steady selling during U.S. market hours since Huang first stepped down. “Bitcoin has fallen in seven of the eight U.S. sessions since Huang went, today’s included, and last week each session’s fall lined up with that day’s ETF outflow,” he said. Crypto stocks keep most of their gains Crypto stocks held up far better than the bitcoin price. Coinbase (COIN) gained about 6.7% to near $108.78, Robinhood (HOOD) rose about 8.8% to near $67.64 and Circle (CRCL) added about 8% to near $51.33. Miners with AI data center businesses posted the biggest moves. IREN (IREN) jumped about 23% to near $14.57, CleanSpark (CLSK) rose about 12.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) gained about 10%. Core Scientific (CORZ) climbed about 9.4% and Riot Platforms (RIOT) added about 7.1%. ETF flows and inflation data are next Monday’s spot bitcoin ETF flows are the next test. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. sports.description: There was a time when an American was in one corner of every single heavyweight world-title fight. Every fight from the end of the bare-knuckle period to the end of the 1980s. The fall of the Wall and the arrival of the Eastern Bloc boxers changed the landscape forever, but still Americans held the grip on a title that seemed forever destined to be owned by a man from Philadelphia or Houston or Louisville. That is all over now, possibly gone for good. Deontay Wilder was the last American heavyweight world champion, and he was beaten in seven rounds by Tyson Fury in early 2020; he challenged Fury the following year, lost again, and that was the last time an American came anywhere near the world heavyweight title. This Saturday, in front of 50,000 fans in Dusseldorf , Germany’s Agit Kabayel defends his WBC heavyweight title when he meets the unbeaten Nelson Hysa of Albania. It is a bizarrely cosmopolitan clash. Kabayel, on his way directly to the WBC title, stopped in succession a Russian, a Chinese fighter, a Croatian, a Pole, and a Cuban. There is not an American heavyweight left to come even close to pushing Kabayel. The top American is arguably a man called Michael Hunter, who is 38 and had his best win in 2018. Hunter is the only American worth a top-20 ranking, and he is lost in a turbulent sea of boxers from a dozen countries. A Nigerian, an Australian and about seven British boxers are in front of Hunter. Where is Rocky Balboa when you need him? Right now, Kabayel might just be the best of the four heavyweight champions, with Daniel Dubois , Filip Hrgovic and Murat Gassiev holding the other belts in the wake of Oleksandr Usyk giving up all of the gold . It will be fun until Kabayel does his thing and breaks Hysa’s heart after about six rounds of body shots. sports.title: The Davis Cup is broken but Carlos Alcaraz can save it
sports.description: For nearly five months of this year, Carlos Alcaraz was sidelined, nursing a wrist injury which threatened to derail his entire season. Just three months on from his return, and despite managing two different injury concerns, the Spaniard has rewritten the history books and could yet send another record tumbling before signing off for Christmas. Four days after claiming his first ATP Finals title, becoming the youngest man – at just 23 – to complete the clean sweep of all four majors and the season-ending individual crown, he could join only Andre Agassi , Novak Djokovic , and Roger Federer in the pantheon of greats to also win the Davis Cup . The tennis calendar doesn’t so much slow to a halt over Christmas as barrel almost cleanly through into the next season, with a rapid turnaround for those heading from the ATP Finals in Turin to the Davis Cup in Bologna this week. But despite Alcaraz’s frenetic autumn schedule, winning three back-to-back tournaments in Vienna, Paris, and Turin, and the wear and tear on his body, he is in spellbinding form and highly fancied to lead Spain to a first title since 2019. The Davis Cup has struggled for relevance in recent years. The fact that it takes place annually lowers the stakes and drama of what claims to be the ‘World Cup’ of tennis, while the torturously convoluted system of play-offs and qualifying ties makes it difficult for the casual fan to understand. Add to that top players’ reluctance to risk injury, and their prioritising of the ATP Tour in an utterly relentless calendar, means the big names tend to drop out and viewers’ interest follows the same downward curve. So it is a huge boost to the tournament that although home star Jannik Sinner remains a long-term absentee, Alcaraz, who missed last year’s Finals, is back, while the Italians – led again by Flavio Cobolli – are fielding a raft of top names including Matteo Berrettini and Lorenzo Musetti . In total, nine top-10 players across both singles and doubles will take part, and seven of the singles top-20. Three-time defending champions Italy face underdogs South Korea before taking on either Felix Auger-Aliassime ’s Canada or Czechia, spearheaded by the top-20 pairing of Jakub Mensik and Jiri Lehecka. technology.description: Troy Hunt, the founder of data breach reporting site Have I Been Pwned (HIBP), has revealed how organizations respond when he informs them they’ve leaked data – if they respond at all. Hunt gave Anthropic’s Claude access to an email inbox containing over eight years of his email correspondence and then asked the AI to write a post summarising them, a method he said “was the best way to highlight the behaviors I keep seeing across many breaches and subsequent disclosure efforts.” Writing in person, Hunt described those behaviors as “standoffish behavior, deliberate delays, heavy involvement from lawyers, and a constant theme: prioritizing corporate interests over those of their customers.” Once Claude takes over writing duties, it opens with the observation that Hunt sent his standard notification email to 73 organizations between March 2018 and November 2026 and also used website contact forms. Claude/Hunt focuses on the breach notifications that don’t go well, for example when first contact “often goes nowhere” because “many organisations have no obvious way to report a security incident.” Some organizations Hunt contacted logged his notifications as customer support requests. “In one case, Troy received three automated surveys asking him to rate the support he'd received,” Claude wrote, before observing “A message that an organization’s customer data is being traded among criminals ended up in the same queue as a question about a late delivery.” Once someone at victim organization gets the message, a common response is to say they can find no evidence of the breach. Others try to play down the incident, saying it was only a website defacement or that Hunt is re-reporting a previous breach the victim has already disclosed. If an organization accepts Hunt is probably onto something, it typically says it needs to investigate the matter. technology.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
technology.description: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws. Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources. Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium , a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project. Cisco and OpenAI think eBPF can help organizations cope with the flood of 100,000-plus software flaws reported this year, many after the debut of AI-powered bug finders. The increased volume of flaws, and patches to fix them, is a problem for many organizations which already struggle to test fixes or find change windows in which to implement them. That problem has seen greater interest in “compensating controls” – changes to applications or infrastructure that harden them against flaws or malware, without requiring a patch. With Shirudo, Cisco and OpenAI are suggesting two things: The privileges eBPF programs enjoy make them a fine way to implement compensating controls for Linux; Agents should scan your infrastructure for vulnerabilities, then use tools like OpenAI’s Codex to write compensating controls as eBPF programs at machine speed. “Shirudo” is apparently the Japanese word for “shield,” so Cisco and OpenAI have called the eBPF programs the tool creates “shields.” The two companies envision humans checking every shield Shirudo creates before putting it into production. Shirudo is open source and available here . The two companies say they’ve already demonstrated it could mitigate the recently discovered flaws in Java without requiring downtime for an Elasticsearch implementation. Cisco and OpenAI are not alone in advocating for compensating controls. Third-party software maintenance outfits like Rimini Street have used them for years to protect software when their clients no longer have the right to access patches. VMware has introduced “virtual patching.” Palo Alto Networks and Rapid 7 also like this approach, and offer automation to develop controls. Where Cisco and OpenAI differ is their decision to make Shirudo open source , and their ambition that other players adapt and advance it. That offer is not entirely altruistic, as if Shirudo takes off it could create more demand for Codex. Cisco’s angle comes from the fact it owns Isovalent, an early champion of eBPF and the creator of both Cilium and the Tetragon sub-project on which Shirudo is based. Switchzilla is using eBPF in other products, so normalizing its use through an open source project can’t hurt. ®

technology.description: The leaders of the great model houses, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman, desperately want the world to believe AI is the skeleton key which will unlock the secrets of the universe. But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box? That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure. In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them. The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2. Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here . What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution. Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros . There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that. Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate. The four pages in which Alpöge remarks on the discoveries he and Claude made aren’t exactly a proof, but rather 14 tarballs worth of Lean code totaling roughly 240 MB. Lean is an open source programming language commonly used to help validate mathematical proofs. technology.title: Inception - possibly a ShinyHunters reboot - claims seven victims in a week
technology.description: Don't mind the recent arrests. The ShinyHunters extortion gang may still be operating, just under the new name of Inception, according to Okta's threat intelligence group. ShinyHunters is the brash cybercriminal group that, most recently, breached rival gang Clop before hacking the FBI , resulting in at least three arrests of key suspects in September and October. The crims - and their old data leak site - have since gone dark. “While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion,” Okta threat hunters Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said on Monday. Okta tracks this threat cluster as O-UNC-053 - the “O-UNC” prefix stands for an Okta Uncategorized cluster, and it uses this label before formally attributing the activity to a named threat group. While Okta hasn't formally confirmed O-UNC-053 to be the same crime crew as ShinyHunters, the identity and access management provider’s researchers note that it does use nearly identical social engineering tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA). Plus, they note: O-UNC-053 operators change the themes of their phishing domains about every four to six weeks, and they also post claimed victims on ShinyHunters’ data leak site. In November, however, organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new data leak site branded as Inception and not ShinyHunters. The first five - Advanced Micro Devices, Cigna Healthcare, Paychex, PepsiCo, and Henry Schein - appeared November 17 on the site, and all were marked “leaked.” Soon after, security maven Dominic Alvieri questioned if Inception was linked to ShinyHunters. “ShinyHunters are not all in jail,” he wrote on social media. On November 19, AutoZone appeared on the site, with Inception again claiming to have leaked the auto-parts retailer's files. On Saturday, EV technology firm Lucid Group joined the claimed victims. None of the seven companies have confirmed breaches, and none responded to The Register ’s inquiries. We will update this story when we receive more information. Okta Threat Intelligence “is unable to validate if published data is authentic,” the researchers said in response to our questions. In the Monday report, the Okta team does note that Inception’s new data leak site listings “included multiple targets for which Okta Threat Intelligence previously observed O-UNC-053 infrastructure registration.” The infrastructure was registered between six and 19 days before Inception listed the companies on its leak site, and this gap “is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors,” Diallo and Nickels added. technology.title: Amazon scoops up AI accelerator tech to keep chips busy at all times
technology.description: Amazon has agreed to buy AI optimization technology from an Israeli startup in a bid to speed up its inference operations. The house of Bezos on Monday announced a deal to purchase proprietary AI acceleration tech from Decart AI, known as the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), for an undisclosed amount. Amazon also plans to bring Decart’s three founders and their engineering team into the fold. Decart’s DOS is designed to push AI hardware closer to its maximum performance across different AI models and hardware platforms. The company claims that most AI chips live their lives without reaching their full potential – practically a sin in this age of increased hardware costs and limited availability – and DOS aims to fix that by operating between the model and the chip, optimizing kernels, compilers, and runtimes for the underlying hardware “so every core stays busy.” DOS is hardware-agnostic, with Decart saying it supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and, most critically for our purposes here, AWS Trainium chips. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost,” Peter DeSantis, Amazon SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, and quantum computing, said in the announcement. “That's the pillar Trainium and our AI efforts are built on, and from our earliest work with Decart, we knew they … would help us push it even further.” Decart doesn’t offer much in the way of details about its proprietary AI-maxxing tech, but claims it can reduce latency, improve throughput, and reduce the costs associated with training and inference runs. An Amazon spokesperson clarified to The Register that the deal is an asset purchase and not a full company acquisition, with Amazon only acquiring DOS and the tech behind it as well as personnel. As for what may become of Decart after the deal, that’s unclear. Amazon told us to reach out to Decart to learn what may happen to any remaining employees and the company’s other technology, but we didn’t hear back. Along with offering its optimization stack, Decart has a couple of different AI models: Lucy, a live video model marketed toward advertisers, live streamers, and the like; and Oasis, a world model AI marketed toward companies working on embodied AI applications. Decart’s non-DOS assets weren’t mentioned in the press release, and per the Amazon spokesperson we talked to, that means they weren’t part of the deal. We can’t imagine that the Decart team is too upset about the potential abandonment of those models, though: While neither company has disclosed a price, Bloomberg claims its sources value the deal at around $7.5 billion. If Bloomberg's figure is accurate, that would make this deal one of the most expensive in Amazon’s history, right between its $3.9 billion acquisition of One Medical and its $8.5 billion purchase of film studio MGM . ®

Signs of unrest began in late October 2026. On October 27, seismic sensors recorded a sharp uptick in activity, and Japan’s Meteorological Agency reported that the first photographs of the eruption were captured. Soon after, sensors on several satellites began to capture an array of observations. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured the left image on October 26, when the coast was still quiet. On November 11, Landsat 9 got its first clear view of the land the submarine volcano has built (right). A shortwave-infrared signature, a sign of the eruption’s heat, is shown in orange. A faint gray volcanic plume drifts southeast of the vent, and a streak of floating pumice stretches across the water in the same direction. A false-color backscatter radar image from the NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite offered an even earlier look at the eruption. On October 28, despite heavy cloud cover, the radar detected a large disturbance in the water in the same area that erupted in December 2023. When the clouds cleared in early November, the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors on NASA and NOAA satellites also captured signs of the ongoing eruption’s volcanic plumes and infrared signature . Japan’s Coast Guard released a report on November 16 confirming the formation of new land connected to the pre-existing beach. The new land adjoins the southeast beach where American troops landed on February 19, 1945, beginning one of the bloodiest battles in the history of the U.S. Marines. The location of the eruption is no surprise to scientists. In addition to the 2023 eruption off the southeast coast, Iwo Jima had an eruption off its west coast in August 2025, said Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. science.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement . "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon." To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith , the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions. The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil. Oregon State University researchers David Handy and Aymeric Goyer studying potatoes grown in lunar regolith. (Image credit: Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/OSU) "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement. The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth. NASA funding supported this research.

science.description:
Alan Bradley is an experienced tech and culture writer with more than 20 years covering gaming, tech, and hardware. He has served as commerce director and in senior editorial roles at major publications. His work has appeared in Rolling Stone, U.S. News & World Report, PCMag, TechRadar, GamesRadar+, CNET, Live Science, Variety, and many other outlets. Alan is also a novelist—his debut novel, the urban fantasy The Sixth Borough, is available now.

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well. "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author. "'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,'" quotes Johnson. "This is very difficult to simulate in real life due to gravity; special effects often try to compensate. With today’s AI and green screens, it can actually look good on screen." In a microgravity scenario, the concept of up and down is no longer relevant. Suddenly, the playing field expands from a single, fixed plane to a fully three-dimensional space that includes height. (Image credit: Netflix) Momentum is also a completely different beast. Instead of being able to quickly stop and pivot the way you can during terrestrial sports, once you start moving in microgravity, you keep going until something stops you. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
science.description: null On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit. The company's triple-core Falcon Heavy boosters can also land vertically and its massive Starship megarocket can even return to the launch site to be caught by giant metal arms. But in the end, Blue Origin did it first. Blue Origin's New Shepard booster landing kicked off an era of vertical launch and vertical landings for rockets that continues to this day. It may have even outlasted the New Shepard rocket. Since that first landing, Blue Origin has launched 17 suborbital astronaut flights with New Shepard, and 21 more uncrewed flights for a total of 38 missions between April 2015 and 2026. The company reused its New Shepard boosters repeatedly (though it did lose one during an uncrewed launch after a technical issue.) But in January 2026, the company announced a pause in New Shepard flights for two years so that it could focus on moon lander projects. But Blue Origin did not abandon rocket landings. Indeed, the company's success with New Shepard led it to build vertical landing into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn, which made its first successful landing 2025 — nearly 10 years after that first touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster , and is developing a new rocket engine called Northstar for even better performance. Want more space history? science.title: NASA Seeks Partners to Design First Nuclear Reactor for the Moon
science.description: Artist’s concept of a nuclear fission power system on the Moon’s surface. Credit: NASA NASA is seeking industry partners to develop and test the first nuclear reactor designed to provide electricity on the Moon, a major step toward establishing a sustained human presence on the lunar surface. Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. For NASA’s plans for a Moon Base , that energy could support future habitats, communications systems, rovers, scientific instruments, and other essential infrastructure. NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment. Unlike solar power, which depends on sunlight, a nuclear reactor can generate electricity continuously, including during the Moon’s approximately two-week-long nights. This capability will enable future lunar operations, particularly in locations where sunlight is limited or unavailable. “This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface,” said Brian Giblin, NASA’s Lunar Reactor-1 program manager. “A reliable source of safe and abundant energy will be vital to future exploration of the lunar and Martian surface. Space nuclear systems will provide continuous power to NASA assets in any environment without dependency on sunlight.” NASA’s Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals incorporates feedback received after the agency released a draft proposal in August and hosted an industry day in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. The solicitation requires that the reactor must meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations. While the primary purpose of the Request for Proposals is to advance the technology, testing, and flight design of LR-1, NASA may issue additional task orders to support the development of other space nuclear power systems. Proposals are due by Dec. 21. Nuclear power will be increasingly important to NASA’s space exploration ambitions. Lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, while dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months. Farther from the Sun, solar power becomes progressively less effective. Nuclear systems offer a reliable source of electricity in these challenging environments. LR-1 is managed by the agency’s Space Reactors Division in partnership with the Department of Energy. The division is also responsible for the development of NASA’s Space Reactor‑1 (SR-1) Freedom. Scheduled to launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom will deliver three SkyFall helicopters to Mars and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion, which uses electricity generated by a nuclear reactor to power spacecraft propulsion systems. science.title: Weird 'potato chips' and 'ghostly rocks' on Mars spotted by NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance
science.description: null NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have spotted a bizarre assortment of Martian oddities, from potato chip-like rocks and ghostly white formations to mysterious patterns etched into the Red Planet's surface. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life. NASA's Curiosity rover recently wrapped up a drilling campaign at a location nicknamed "Nazca," where scientists have been examining unusual disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in the surrounding bedrock. Some of the features are so thin and flat that the mission team likened them to potato chips, according to a statement from the space agency. NASA's Curiosity rover captured a close-up view of unusual, disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in Martian bedrock using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) on Nov. 7, 2026 (Sol 5067). The thin, flattened formations resemble tiny potato chips. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) Curiosity used its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), mounted on the end of its robotic arm, to capture detailed close-up images of the formations on Nov. 7 — the rover's 5,067th Martian day , or Sol 5067. The rover also used its ChemCam instrument to study the rocks' chemical composition, while samples from the Nazca drill site were delivered to its onboard Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) instrument for further analysis. Meanwhile, NASA's Perseverance rover has been investigating a collection of unusually bright rocks in an area called "Idubi," located in the “Lac de Charmes” region outside Jezero Crater. The rover captured images of the formations on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), revealing pale, ghostly-looking rocks that stand out dramatically against the darker, dust-covered Martian landscape. Data from Perseverance's SuperCam instrument revealed that the rocks are rich in hydrated silica rather than being typical igneous rocks. That discovery has scientists particularly interested. On Earth, hydrated silica can form in environments involving hydrothermal activity or groundwater. These deposits are also capable of preserving microscopic fossils, making them valuable targets in the search for evidence of ancient life, according to another statement from NASA. Avengers: Doomsday has been promising the scale and excitement the MCU has often been lacking since the Infinity Saga. science.description: null An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, produced by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains. Despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers). Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, as seen by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Why is it incredible? While Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported . In addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material. The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past. By studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

science.description: A closing plenary session at the COP31 climate summit on 22 November AP Photo/Khalil Hamra/Alamy A deep rift among nations on how to tackle climate change, and whether the global economy can be weaned off fossil fuels, was exposed after the spectacular collapse of talks at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. After a tortuous fortnight of negotiations, COP31 ended in disarray late on 22 November after countries including the UK and the EU refused to agree to a political accord that failed to mention fossil fuels. Read more Can everyone live a ‘good life’ without destroying the planet? The Antalya pact would have seen countries officially recognise that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C degrees of warming and promise to limit the scale of the overshoot as far as possible. It also would have committed nations to increasing the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 per cent globally by 2035, a key target for climate campaigners who see electrification as the route away from fossil-fuel dependency. Advertisement But the draft agreement proved unacceptable to many countries, including the UK, the EU and some small island nations, after all mentions of fossil fuels were omitted at the behest of fossil fuel-dependent nations such as Saudi Arabia and Russia. Failing to mention fossil fuels explicitly in the text would have marked a backwards step for the climate process, the EU argued. At COP28 in Dubai three years ago, nations agreed to “transition away from fossil fuels” , but since then, attempts to strengthen the language or clarify how this transition will take place have been blocked by petrostates. Alden Meyer at the climate think tank E3G says the talks were subjected to a “brutish” strategy from fossil fuel-exporting states to “systematically block” any reference to the COP28 deal. “They clearly have buyer’s remorse about that agreement. They never were happy about it.” Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter The EU also took issue with a paragraph inserted at the behest of Saudi Arabia – which leads the 22-member Arab group of countries – calling for the rapid growth of carbon capture and storage technologies to the gigatonne scale by 2035. Carbon capture and storage technologies are expensive and unproven at scale, and many sceptics are concerned that focusing on them will justify the continued use of fossil fuels and distract from the deep emissions cuts necessary for controlling climate change. Ireland’s climate minister Darragh O’ Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU, claimed the negotiations had been “hijacked by fossil fuel producers” and said the EU would “not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels”. science.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure? Last of the Soviet space explorers Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June. The stakes were almost immediately raised as Phobos 2 arrived in orbit around Mars on Jan. 30, 1989 , when one of the probe's three onboard flight system processors was found to have gone offline, with another already experiencing technical issues.
